extracted.intended_audience: authors of health research articles, journal editors, peer reviewers, and reporting guideline developers
extracted.subtask_description: Locate and select appropriate reporting guidelines and related policy documents for health research reporting (by study type, specialty, language, and development status). The page is an index of guidelines, resources, and metadata to guide authors, editors and peer reviewers toward the correct reporting standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidelines for randomised trials (CONSORT)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting randomised trials, use the CONSORT guideline and relevant CONSORT extensions; consult the Library for core checklist items and extensions relevant to trial design and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidelines for observational studies (STROBE)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies, follow STROBE and any applicable extensions to ensure complete transparent reporting of study design, participants, variables, bias, study size, and statistical methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidelines for systematic reviews (PRISMA)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors of systematic reviews should follow PRISMA and relevant extensions (e.g., for protocols, abstracts, individual participant data) to report search methods, selection, data extraction, synthesis and reporting biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidelines for study protocols (SPIRIT, PRISMA-P)
rubrics_metrics.description: Study protocols — SPIRIT; PRISMA-P for systematic review protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing study or review protocols, use SPIRIT (for clinical trial protocols) or PRISMA-P (for systematic review protocols) to describe objectives, methods, outcomes, and governance transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidelines for diagnostic/prognostic studies (STARD, TRIPOD)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For studies of diagnostic accuracy and prognostic models, use STARD (diagnostic accuracy) or TRIPOD (prediction model development/validation) to report participants, index tests, reference standards, model specification, performance and validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidelines for case reports (CARE)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors reporting individual case reports or case series should use the CARE guideline to ensure essential clinical details, patient perspective (where appropriate), diagnostic assessment, interventions, and outcomes are reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidelines for clinical practice guidelines (AGREE, RIGHT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical practice guidelines — AGREE and RIGHT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developers and reporters of clinical practice guidelines should consult AGREE and RIGHT to ensure transparent development processes, evidence appraisal, recommendations, and implementation considerations are described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidelines for qualitative research (SRQR, COREQ)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For qualitative studies, follow SRQR or COREQ to report study design, researcher reflexivity, data collection and analysis methods, and findings with sufficient contextualisation and evidence (e.g., quotations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidelines for animal pre-clinical studies (ARRIVE)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report in vivo animal research using ARRIVE to cover ethical approvals, experimental conditions, allocation, blinding, outcome measures, statistical methods, and reproducibility-related details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidelines for quality improvement studies (SQUIRE)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SQUIRE for reporting quality improvement initiatives, including context, intervention details, study of the intervention, measures, analysis, and lessons learned to aid replication and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidelines for economic evaluations (CHEERS)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economic evaluation reports should follow CHEERS to ensure transparent reporting of perspective, comparators, costs, outcomes, time horizon, discounting, and sensitivity analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use translations of reporting guidelines when available
rubrics_metrics.description: Some reporting guidelines are also available in languages other than English. See the Translations section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appropriate, use translated versions of reporting guidelines to support authors and reviewers working in other languages; consult the Library's Translations section for available resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult reporting guidelines under development
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting guidelines under development — listings of guidelines not yet finalised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of and consult guidelines in development that may apply to novel study designs or emerging methods; check the Library's section for works-in-progress to anticipate forthcoming standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult the EQUATOR reporting guideline manual
rubrics_metrics.description: EQUATOR Network reporting guideline manual — methodological guidance on using and developing guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the EQUATOR reporting guideline manual for instructions on how to find, apply, and develop reporting guidelines and for advice on implementation and dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use supplementary guidance resources (scientific writing, editorial guidance, funder requirements, ethics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional guidance categories: Guidance on scientific writing; Guidance developed by editorial groups; Research funders’ guidance on reporting requirements; Research ethics, publication ethics and good practice guidelines; Professional medical writing support; Links to other resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond core reporting checklists, consult writing guidance, editorial policies, funder reporting requirements, ethical and publication best-practice documents, and professional writing support resources to align manuscript content with stakeholder expectations and obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library scope, content identification and inclusion/exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: For information about Library scope and content, identification of reporting guidelines and inclusion/exclusion criteria please visit About the Library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the Library's About page for the scope and criteria used to select and include reporting guidelines, to understand the coverage and limitations of the collection when choosing resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended audience for Library resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Library resources are aimed mainly at authors of research articles, journal editors, peer reviewers and reporting guideline developers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select resources and guidance targeted to your role (author, editor, reviewer, developer) to find the most relevant instructions and checklists for preparing, evaluating, or developing reports.
